current_example.title: Example: Expressing a Fraction as a Power With a Negative Exponent

q-175985.name: Question 1
q-175985.problem: Expressed as a fraction in its simplest form, ${4}^{-4}=${{field-1}}.
q-175985.worked_solution:
We find the reciprocal of the base $(4),$ and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the *opposite* sign $(+4),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{-4} & ={(\frac{1}{4})}^{4} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4})\times (\frac{1}{4})\times (\frac{1}{4})\times (\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =(\frac{1\times 1\times 1\times 1}{4\times 4\times 4\times 4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{256}\end{aligned}
$$

q-6197.name: Question 2
q-6197.worked_solution:
We find the reciprocal of the base $(4),$ and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the *opposite* sign $(+3),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{-3} & ={(\frac{1}{4})}^{3} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4})\times (\frac{1}{4})\times (\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =(\frac{1\times 1\times 1}{4\times 4\times 4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{64}\end{aligned}
$$

q-173748.name: Question 3
q-173748.problem: Expressed as a whole number or fraction in its simplest form, ${(\frac{1}{10})}^{-3}=${{field-1}}.
q-173748.worked_solution:
We find the reciprocal of the base $(\frac{1}{10}),$ and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the *opposite* sign $(+3),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{1}{10})}^{-3} & =(10)^{3} \\  & =10\cdot 10\cdot 10 \\  & =1,000\end{aligned}
$$

q-128675.name: Question 5
q-128675.problem: Express $\frac{9}{4}$ as a base raised to a negative exponent.
q-128675.worked_solution:
First, we write $\frac{9}{4}$ as a base raised to a power:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{4} & =\frac{3\times 3}{2\times 2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\times \frac{3}{2} \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the reciprocal of the base $(\frac{3}{2}),$ and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the *opposite* sign $(-2),$ as follows:

$$
{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}={(\frac{2}{3})}^{-2}
$$

q-128675.html:
Question 5
?

Express 94 as a base raised to a negative exponent.

a
(23)−2
b
−(23)2
c
(23)2
d
−(23)−2
e
(32)−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write 94 as a base raised to a power:

94=3×32×2=32×32=(32)2

Now, we find the reciprocal of the base (32), and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the opposite sign (−2), as follows: (32)2=(23)−2

q-128737.name: Question 6
q-128737.problem: Express $\frac{36}{25}$ as a base raised to a negative exponent.
q-128737.worked_solution:
First, we write $\frac{36}{25}$ as a base raised to a power:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{36}{25} & =\frac{6\times 6}{5\times 5} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\times \frac{6}{5} \\  & ={(\frac{6}{5})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the reciprocal of the base $(\frac{6}{5}),$ and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the *opposite* sign $(-2),$ as follows:

$$
{(\frac{6}{5})}^{2}={(\frac{5}{6})}^{-2}
$$

a
 (65)−2
b
 −(56)−2

 (56)2
d
(56)−2
e
